subject: Tenant-bound data guarantees review for Dedicated — Crestpoint
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@crestpoint.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: security@crestpoint.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: residency & deletion guarantees for Dedicated deployment

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Crestpoint is excited about Redwood Dedicated. Before we move into contract discussions, InfoSec and Legal have a couple of specific asks we need written confirmation on:

1) Region pinning: Can we pin a Dedicated tenancy to a single geographic region (us-west-2) for all model data, logs, and snapshots?
2) Physical/tenant isolation: Please confirm whether backups/snapshots and any stored KV caches are tenant-scoped (no cross-tenant co-mingling).
3) Deletion / erasure SLA: Once we request a tenant wipe, what is the maximum time to full data destruction across primary storage, backups, and any control-plane artifacts? We need a timeframe we can include in the contract.
4) Audit evidence: Do you provide a deletion attestations package (runbook, hashes, ops tickets) suitable for our audit and legal team?

Can you respond with concrete timelines and any supporting artifacts we can share with legal? We are targeting a procurement decision by end of month so a quick turnaround would be appreciated.

Best,
Elena
Senior Security Manager
Crestpoint Bank

[Attachment: crestpoint-security-reqs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@crestpoint.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: residency & deletion guarantees for Dedicated deployment

Hi Elena — great to hear from you. Thanks for laying out the asks clearly. Below are concrete answers and next steps; I’ve looped in Hannah (security/compliance) and Marcus (ops) for any technical clarifications and to surface the runbooks.

Summary answers (high level):
- Region pinning: Yes. A Dedicated tenancy can be pinned to a single AWS region (we commonly do us-west-2). All customer data for that tenancy — model inputs, embeddings, KV caches, and persistent snapshots/backups — are stored in the pinned region by default.
- Tenant isolation: Storage is tenant-scoped. Snapshots and persistent artifacts are tagged and isolated at the tenant level; no multi-tenant co-mingling of customer blobs or KV namespaces.
- Deletion SLA: We offer a two-stage erasure process: a) logical deletion that removes access and marks data for purge within 24 hours, b) physical purge from primary storage and deletion of tenant snapshots within 72 hours. For backups, if cross-region replication is not enabled, backups are deleted within the same 72-hour window; if replication was enabled, wipe of replicas follows the same 72-hour SLA after we confirm the replica locations.
- Audit evidence: We can provide a standardized deletion attestation bundle (runbook excerpt, ops ticket id, checksum list, and time-stamped audit log slice).

Attached: region-pin-playbook.pdf (high-level runbook and architecture), tenant-wipe-runbook.pdf (operational checklist). I’ll also prepare a short attestation template Legal can reference for contract language.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm that Crestpoint wants region pinning to us-west-2 and that cross-region replication will NOT be enabled for this tenancy (this avoids the extra replication wipe step).
2) If agreed, I’ll issue an official attestation doc and we can include an SLA clause: "tenant data and backups will be fully purged within 72 hours of confirmed request."
3) Hannah/Marcus to coordinate a short verification exercise (we can run a tenant wipe in a staging tenancy and capture the attestation artifacts) — let us know a preferred window.

If you’d like, we can put the attestation and an appendix into the SOW/Exhibit for the contract.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: region-pin-playbook.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: tenant-wipe-runbook.pdf (pdf)]

Aditya — thanks for the quick response, this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from Legal/Procurement:

- Backups: please confirm that, by default, snapshots/backups are kept in the pinned region and that cross-region backups are opt-in only. We need explicit confirmation to avoid ambiguous contract language.
- Control-plane logs: we need to understand what evidence remains in Redwood's control plane (audit logs, telemetry). If those are stored outside the pinned region, we’ll need a clear retention policy and the option for region-local audit bundles.

Also, Legal asked whether you can provide a short, signable attestation (1-2 pages) that we can attach to the contract exhibiting the 72-hour purge promise. If you can provide that plus the runbook excerpts that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@crestpoint.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: residency & deletion guarantees for Dedicated deployment

Hi Elena — Hannah from Security here. Short answers to the follow-ups and a proposed mitigation path.

- Backups: Confirmed — snapshots/backups for a Dedicated tenancy remain in the pinned region by default. Cross-region replication is an explicit configuration step and requires customer opt-in. We will mark that as a material change in the SOW if enabled.
- Snapshot metadata: Logical metadata (indexing entries used by the control plane) is retained in the control plane to support operations, but we provide a region-local snapshot archive that contains full metadata necessary for legal audit. For customers requiring that metadata never leave the region, we offer a private-control-plane option that keeps control-plane data inside the customer VPC/region (this is part of Redwood Private).
- Control-plane logs & telemetry: By default, lightweight operational telemetry (health metrics, anonymized traces) is retained in our control plane for 90 days to support reliability and debugging. However, for Dedicated customers with contractual residency requirements we can:
   a) Provide a region-local audit bundle on-demand (time-stamped slices of logs relevant to the wipe)
   b) Offer a longer-term option to ship audit logs to the customer’s storage in the pinned region (S3 export) as part of the contract.

I’ve attached a one-page retention_matrix.xlsx that maps artifact types (snapshots, KV cache, logs, control-plane index) to default retention and our configurable options. Marcus — can you confirm the operational steps and the exact ticket pattern we will use for attestations?

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Security, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
